title: What Will it Take to Fix Benchmarking in Natural Language Understanding?

bias_targets.methodology: The paper is a position piece and does not empirically measure bias itself. Instead, it advocates for evaluating general social biases by introducing a family of auxiliary, expert-constructed test datasets and metrics that isolate and penalize specific biases alongside primary NLU benchmarks.

Discussed theoretically as a primary candidate for auxiliary evaluation; the authors propose incorporating existing test sets like Winogender into standard benchmark reporting to penalize models that rely on gender heuristics.
Discussed theoretically; the authors highlight the need to measure biased associations in word representations, specifically between typical Black/White names and professional occupation terms.

Highlighted conceptually as a salient, culturally specific social attribute (Indian castes) that demonstrates the complexity of enumerating social biases and the need for adaptable, context-aware bias evaluation metrics.
